meta.title: Precision housings: make, lease or buy in 2027
meta.subtitle: Executive committee decision, January 2027
meta.purpose: Decide whether to make precision housings in-house in 2027, lease a flexible cell, or keep buying
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack

storyline.governing_thought: Keep buying housings in 2027, add a qualified second source and hold the leased cell as a gated option for 2028; the owned cell cannot be funded within the board's limits

exec_summary.text: Like for like, the owned cell's $27 saving per housing shrinks to about $1.70

sub_points.text: Operating savings repay only 78% of the $7.3M outlay by 2029
Over 2027–29 the owned cell saves $0.51M and the lease $0.30M

exec_summary.text: The owned cell breaks the board's limits, and the lease needs near-full demand

sub_points.text: The $7.3M outlay tops the $5.0M limit and leaves only $1.9M of cash
On conservative demand the lease loses $1.4M, 4.6 times its upside

exec_summary.text: Delivery, not insourcing, is the mandate; a second source protects it at lower cost

sub_points.text: On-time delivery sits just under 97%, hurt by one flood closure
Four layers, from a second shop to reserved capacity, cover an outage

exec_summary.text: Buy with a second source in 2027 and switch to the lease only if a trigger fires

sub_points.text: A 2028 lease is a near tie; orders, price or delivery would tip it
Renew the supplier contract before the quote lapses in March 2027

next_steps.action: Approve buying for 2027 and the $250K alternate-shop tooling; decline the owned-cell capital request
Renew the supplier contract with split quarterly orders, 40,000 reserved units and indicative 2028–29 prices
Commission the lessor's site survey on power and ventilation, with no commitment to lease
Model buffer-stock carrying cost and re-measure on-time delivery on the contract's requested-units basis
Review the three lease triggers against confirmed 2028 orders and the renewed supplier price

constraints.item: $5.0M limit on new 2027 capital spending without a new financing agreement
constraints.effect: the owned cell's $7.3M breaks it; lease installation counted against it and fits

constraints.item: Year-end unrestricted cash above $4.0M, from $9.2M today, no new debt or equity
constraints.effect: the owned cell would leave $1.9M before other cash flows; the plan leaves $8.26M

constraints.item: Supplier paid on accepted units; cells pay for scrap on every start (8% and 6% in 2027, 4% after)
constraints.effect: scrap and like-for-like unit costs are in every cost number

constraints.item: Fixed costs, upfront installation and $2 freight that the CFO's slide left out
constraints.effect: they are the bridge from $27 to $1.70 per housing

constraints.item: Nine-month equipment lead time and five-month lease deployment
constraints.effect: the model assumes full-year 2027 output for both cells, which flatters them; titles say savings are thin even so and footnotes flag it

constraints.item: Supplier quote lapses in March 2027 and assumes the current specification; later prices are indicative
constraints.effect: renewal before March is the first action; the price trigger covers a higher renewal

constraints.item: Alternate shop's unit price is not in the briefing pack
constraints.effect: the plan splits orders only after the shop quotes; the $0.25M tooling is shown as the second source's cost against plain buying

constraints.item: Supplier price after March 2027 is indicative, with no take-or-pay
constraints.effect: a 2028 lease is a near tie at $75 on plan volume; the price trigger and the $80 midpoint show how fast it tips

constraints.item: Buffer-stock carrying cost not modelled; unquantified loss if the customer designation is lost
constraints.effect: the plan's cash includes the stock's value but not its carrying cost; both are named on the slides and in next steps

alternatives.option: Lease the flexible cell now: it fits both limits, deploys in five months and saves $0.30M on planning demand
alternatives.why: the saving is 1.3% of purchases and turns into a $1.38M loss on conservative demand; break-even needs 96% of an unguaranteed forecast. Kept as a prepared option with triggers

alternatives.option: Keep buying without the alternate-shop tooling, relying on buffer stock, $88 emergency orders and reserved units
alternatives.why: it keeps the one-shop dependency the customer audit flagged; the $0.25M tooling costs about two six-week emergency orders at the $13 premium

alternatives.option: Phased owned cell: a smaller first capital request within the $5.0M limit
alternatives.why: the pack gives no phased equipment costs, the full cell saves only $0.51M with resale, and the nine-month lead time means no 2027 output; the lease is the cheaper staged route to in-house capacity

failure_threshold.driver: committed 2028–29 volume and the renewed supplier price
failure_threshold.threshold: a 2028 lease beats buying above about 222,000 good units in 2028–29 (220,000 planned) or, even on conservative demand, above about $86 per delivered housing
failure_threshold.range: lease saving compared with buying, 2027–29: low −$1.38M (conservative), base +$0.30M (planning), +$0.06M if scrap stays at 6%; the pack has no demand case above plan

consistency.headline: Keep buying housings in 2027, add a qualified second source and hold the leased cell as a gated option for 2028; the owned cell cannot be funded within the board's limits
consistency.fix: Governing thought changed from 'drop the owned cell' to 'cannot be funded within the board's limits'; the supplier title no longer compares the orders-based 96.8% with the units-based 97% as a like-for-like gap; the trigger title admits a 2028 lease is a near tie at plan volume

body.assumptions_header: The margin above break-even is thin, and every assumption cuts toward it
assumptions: Planning demand of 300,000 is only 4.5% above break-even; the conservative 230,000 reaches 80% of it
The supplier's $75 delivered price holds for three years, though it is quoted only to March 2027
Lease scrap falls from 6% to 4% after 2027; if it stays at 6%, the three-year saving drops to $0.06M
The lease runs all of 2027; a five-month deployment after a site survey means fewer units to spread its costs over

footnotes: Break-even = costs to recover ÷ saving per good unit; 2027 scrap premium = 80,000 × ($52.13 − $51.04). Planning demand clears break-even by only about 13,000 units
